# TeamPulse Workflow Governance Checklist: Work Intake and Tracking

**Purpose**: Review whether the TeamPulse work-intake requirements clearly define workflow transitions, authorization boundaries, and auditable change history.
**Created**: 2026-08-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 - Are the allowed request states and valid transitions explicitly defined for the full lifecycle from intake through closure? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK002 - Are the request categories and their operational meaning clearly defined for feature, bug, technical debt, and incident intake? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK003 - Are the required metadata fields for each request fully enumerated and consistent with intake, review, and audit needs? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK004 - Is the meaning of "priority" defined in a way that can be interpreted consistently by authorized reviewers and assignees? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK005 - Is the distinction between status updates and priority changes clearly defined for actors and approval rules? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK006 - Is the scope of "important changes" in the audit trail quantified to avoid ambiguity in which events are retained? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK007 - Do authorization requirements align across creation, reassignment, status changes, and priority changes without creating conflicting policy boundaries? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §FR-007, §FR-013]
- [x] CHK008 - Do lifecycle states and acceptance scenarios align with the documented operational workflow without contradictory paths or alternate interpretations? [Consistency, User Stories, Spec §FR-008]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK009 - Are primary intake and assignment flows covered for feature, bug, technical debt, and incident requests across the expected user roles? [Coverage, User Story 1]
- [x] CHK010 - Are alternate and exception paths defined for blocked updates, invalid transitions, and unauthorized change attempts? [Coverage, Edge Cases, Spec §FR-007]
- [ x] CHK011 - Are recovery or closure paths defined for resolved and closed requests without ambiguous end-state behaviors? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK012 - Are requirements defined for invalid status transitions, unsupported priorities, and reassignment conflicts when the workflow policy is violated? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [x] CHK013 - Are assumptions about team roles, designated approvers, and request visibility documented where policy decisions are delegated? [Assumption, Gap]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK014 - Are operational assumptions about ownership, authorization, and escalation paths documented and reviewable before implementation starts? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK015 - Are dependencies on permissions, assignment ownership, and audit retention clearly identified so downstream implementation and review can remain aligned? [Dependency, Gap]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK016 - Are the operational requirements for request visibility, access latency, and history retrieval defined with measurable expectations? [Non-Functional, Spec §SC-003]
- [x] CHK017 - Are reliability requirements defined for audit history retention, including what happens if a change is not recorded or cannot be persisted? [Non-Functional, Gap]
- [x] CHK018 - Are security and privacy requirements for request visibility, ownership, and audit data explicitly defined for sensitive work items? [Non-Functional, Spec §FR-007]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK019 - Are requirements clear about whether role names are global or team-scoped across multiple engineering groups? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK020 - Are any conflicting assumptions about who may close a request versus who may resolve it explicitly documented and reconciled? [Conflict, Gap]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline when a requirement needs further clarification.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
